blocks.content: Lakshadweep's demography is defined by two exceptional, frequently tested superlatives: it is India's smallest UT/state by population, and it has by far the highest Muslim population share of any Indian state or UT.

cells: approx 96-97% — the highest proportion of any Indian state or UT
Nearly the entire native population is classified as Scheduled Tribe — one of the highest ST population shares of any Indian territory
approx 91-92% — among the highest of any Indian state/UT
approx 946 females per 1,000 males — comparatively favourable relative to the national average

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Lakshadweep's ~96-97% Muslim population share is the HIGHEST of any Indian state or UT — a frequently tested superlative, alongside its very high literacy rate (~91-92%), which is unusually high for such a remote, small territory.

items: Lakshadweep's indigenous social structure has historically followed a matrilineal system (property and lineage traced through the maternal line) among most island communities — a distinctive social pattern shared with certain communities of the Kerala mainland (notably some Nair and Muslim/Mappila communities), reflecting the islands' deep historical and cultural ties to Kerala.

This matrilineal tradition, while it has evolved and diminished in strict practice over recent decades in line with wider modernisation trends, remains a distinctive and specifically tested aspect of Lakshadweep's traditional social organisation, setting it apart from the patrilineal norms more common across most of mainland India.

Minicoy Island (Chapter 1) has its own distinct social structure and administrative tradition, organised historically around a unique clan/lineage-based system with its own council structure ('Ameen'-led administration), reflecting its closer cultural proximity to the Maldives than to the rest of Lakshadweep.

Malayalam is the majority language across most of Lakshadweep (Amindivi and Laccadive groups), reflecting the islands' historical settlement from and administrative ties to the Kerala mainland (Chapter 2), and is written in the Malayalam script.

Mahl (related to the Divehi/Thaana script tradition), the language of Minicoy Island, is linguistically distinct from Malayalam — it is closely related to Dhivehi, the national language of the Maldives, and is traditionally written in a script related to the Maldivian Thaana script, reflecting Minicoy's closer cultural and linguistic proximity to the Maldives than to the rest of Lakshadweep.
This linguistic distinction (Malayalam across most islands vs. Mahl on Minicoy) is a frequently tested internal-diversity fact about a UT otherwise often assumed to be linguistically uniform.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Minicoy Island's language, Mahl, is closely related to Dhivehi (the Maldives' national language) — NOT to Malayalam, which is the majority language everywhere else in Lakshadweep. This Minicoy-vs-rest-of-Lakshadweep linguistic distinction is a favourite exam trap.

items: Population (2011): approx 64,473 — India's smallest state/UT by population.
~96-97% Muslim population — the highest share of any Indian state/UT; nearly entire native population is Scheduled Tribe.
Literacy rate ~91-92% — among the highest of any Indian state/UT.
Matrilineal social traditions historically prevalent, shared with parts of Kerala's social structure.
Malayalam = majority language (most islands); Mahl (related to Maldivian Dhivehi) = language of Minicoy Island specifically.
